# cortexcloud_indicator (Resource)

Manages a single Indicator of Compromise (IOC) in Cortex. Backed by the upsert `/public_api/v1/indicators/insert` endpoint: every edit submits the server-assigned `rule_id` carried in state so the API overwrites the existing record in place. A rename (a change to the `indicator` value itself) is just another field update on that `rule_id`, so it preserves the record's identity rather than recreating it.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `indicator` (String) The IOC value (hash, IP, domain, filename, or path). Unique per tenant. Changes are applied in place via the `rule_id`-keyed upsert path — the same path used for every other field — so `rule_id` is preserved across a rename.
- `severity` (String) Indicator severity. Documented values come from `enums.IndicatorSeverities()` — the namespaced `SEV_NNN_X` form the live API accepts on both reads and writes.
- `type` (String) Indicator type. Documented values come from `enums.IndicatorTypes()`.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment.
- `default_expiration_enabled` (Boolean) When true, the indicator uses the tenant default expiration policy for its type instead of `expiration_date`.
- `expiration_date` (Number) Unix epoch milliseconds at which the IOC expires. Use `-1` for `Never`. Required by the API; defaults to `-1` when omitted.
- `reliability` (String) Reliability rating. Documented values come from `enums.IndicatorReliabilities()` (A most reliable through G least); the empty string means unset.
- `reputation` (String) Indicator reputation. Documented values come from `enums.IndicatorReputations()`.

### Read-Only

- `creation_time` (Number) Unix epoch milliseconds when the indicator was first created. Stable across updates, including a rename, since the record is upserted in place rather than recreated.
- `id` (String) Mirror of `indicator`; the resource identity used for state addressing. Computed so a rename of `indicator` legitimately updates this value rather than violating the plan-vs-apply invariant.
- `modification_time` (Number) Unix epoch milliseconds of the most recent update.
- `number_of_issues` (Number) Count of issues this indicator has fired on. Server-maintained.
- `rule_id` (Number) Server-assigned numeric ID — the record's canonical identity. The upsert path keys on this value, so it is stable across every update, including a rename of the `indicator` string.
- `source` (String) Human-readable origin of the most recent write — typically `Public API user (key #<id>)` for API-key-authored records, or a user email for UI/SSO-authored records. Useful for detecting out-of-band drift.
- `status` (String) Server-reported status (e.g. `ENABLED`).
